vaers.name: Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS)
vaers.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
vaers.description:
Established in 1990, the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) is a national early warning system co-managed by the CDC and FDA to detect possible safety problems in U.S.-licensed vaccines. It is a passive reporting system that accepts reports of adverse events following vaccination from anyone, including healthcare providers, vaccine manufacturers, and the public; certain providers and all manufacturers are required to report. VAERS is not designed to determine whether a vaccine caused a health problem, but is useful for detecting unusual or unexpected patterns ("safety signals") that may warrant further investigation through systems such as the Vaccine Safety Datalink (VSD), CISA, and FDA BEST.

VAERS data have important limitations: the number of reports alone cannot establish a causal association or the existence, severity, frequency, or rates of vaccine-related problems. Reports may be incomplete, inaccurate, coincidental, unverified, or biased, and generally reflect only initial report data without medical-record follow-up. Data cover reports received from 1990 to the present and should be interpreted alongside other scientific information.
